rationale: The literature supports phenotypic divergence across TUBA4A variants. Whereas TUBA4A variants were initially identified in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and frontotemporal dementia (FTDALS9/ALS22), distinct heterozygous missense variants (such as p.Glu415Lys and other ultra-rare missense changes) cause autosomal dominant spastic ataxia 11 (SPAX11) with variable age of onset and cerebellar ataxia with spasticity, without classic lower motor neuron degeneration. Patient-derived fibroblasts harboring SPAX11 variants demonstrate distinct alterations in microtubule dynamics and organization. An in vivo animal model (Tuba4a Q176P) further validates this divergence, exhibiting selective Purkinje cell degeneration and skeletal myopathy (SPAX11/CMYO26 phenotypes) while explicitly lacking motor neuron loss.

evidence.text: Screening of 448 probands with cerebellar ataxia and analysis of the 100,000 Genomes Project identified 12 patients from 11 families with predicted pathogenic TUBA4A missense variants causing spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia with variable age of onset. Microtubule organization and dynamics were significantly impaired in patient fibroblasts, confirming TUBA4A as a spastic ataxia gene distinct from ALS phenotypes.

source.title: De novo and inherited monoallelic variants in TUBA4A cause ataxia and spasticity
source.quote: Screening a multicentric French cohort of 448 unrelated probands presenting with cerebellar ataxia, we identified ultra-rare TUBA4A missense variants... gene burden analyses in the 100 000 Genomes project (100KGP) showed enrichment of TUBA4A rare variants in the inherited ataxia group compared to controls [odds ratio: 57.0847 (10.2-576.7); P = 4.02 ×10-7]. Taken together, we report 12 patients presenting with spasticity and/or cerebellar ataxia... Cultured fibroblasts from three patients harbouring distinct TUBA4A missense showed significant alterations in microtubule organization and dynamics

evidence.text: Identification of two independent families (one containing 11 affected members and another sporadic case) carrying the TUBA4A p.Glu415Lys variant revealed a spastic ataxia phenotype (SPAX11) distinct from previously reported TUBA4A-associated motor neuron diseases.

source.title: A new genetic cause of spastic ataxia: the p.Glu415Lys variant in TUBA4A
source.quote: In the present study, we report two families, one with 11 affected individuals and the other with a single patient, carrying a novel, likely pathogenic, variant (p. Glu415Lys) in the TUBA4A gene (NM_006000). The phenotype, not previously described, is that of spastic ataxia.

evidence.text: A dominant missense mutation in Tuba4a (p.Gln176Pro) produces ataxia, Purkinje cell degeneration, and skeletal myopathy without lower or upper motor neuron loss, demonstrating cell-type selective vulnerability and divergence from ALS.

source.title: A mouse model of autosomal dominant spastic ataxia and myopathy caused by a mutation in Tuba4a
source.quote: Mutant mice are normal at 3 weeks... by 30 days these mice have overt ataxia, Purkinje neuron degeneration, and extensive skeletal muscle defects... Our mice exhibit hallmark features of SPAX11 and CMYO26, but do not show motor neuron degeneration.

new_directions.question_text: Does structural position on the alpha/beta-tubulin intradimer versus interdimer contact interface dictate whether a TUBA4A mutation causes selective Purkinje degeneration (SPAX11), primary myopathy (CMYO26), or motor neuron loss (FTDALS9)?
new_directions.rationale: Mapping all published variants across the 3D tubulin lattice will reveal whether dominant-negative destabilization of the dimer interface triggers motor neuron death whereas surface-exposed microtubule-binding interface variants alter transport dynamics causing cerebellar and spastic signs.

new_directions.question_text: What is the true penetrance and expressivity of the recurrent p.Glu415Lys variant across diverse non-European cohorts presenting with hereditary spastic paraplegia or spinocerebellar ataxia?
new_directions.rationale: Identifying the phenotypic range across large global ataxia registries will clarify whether subclinical upper motor neuron signs or myopathy coexist in SPAX11 carriers.
